turns.text: Hey, nice to hear from you. How are you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want to get into photography, and I'm stuck choosing my first camera.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Let me get through all the options before you weigh in.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The first one is a used entry level camera with a kit lens, cheap and good for learning.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then there's a new compact mirrorless camera that's small and light but costs a lot more.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Option three is skipping a camera and just buying a nicer phone with a great camera.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And the last one is an old film camera from a thrift store, which sounds fun but pricey to develop.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's the full list. Go ahead.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: For learning the basics, the used entry level camera is a smart, low risk start. The mirrorless camera is great if you'll carry it everywhere, since small cameras actually get used. A good phone is easiest, but you won't learn manual controls as well.
